speaker_role: college admissions professional presenting at a boarding school; has worked at six institutions (appears to be admissions staff/counselor, exact role unclear)
key_insights: Students should treat the college search as their own research project and own the process, with adults advising rather than driving.
Do a self-assessment first: intended academics, learning environment, class size, and list must-have 'deal makers' and 'deal breakers'.
Do not fixate on choosing a major; being undeclared is fine, and current students often change fields.
Be wary of hearsay and rankings; the speaker considers rankings arbitrary and prefers fit, outcomes and career-services data.
Aim for a list of roughly six to eight schools with good fits and a couple of reasonable reaches.
Use free search tools (Naviance, College Board search, a federal site) with filters like size, region, major and affordability.
Avoid procrastination and keep communication open with parents so senior year is not consumed by applications.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker cites nearly 4,000 US colleges and universities.
Speaker recommends a list of 6 to 8 schools.
Speaker mentions a federal affordability filter example of $20,000 or fewer (vaguely recalled).
notable_or_distinctive: Mostly motivational, family-oriented talk with 'college choice matters less than what you do there' framing; generic.
reliability_notes: Very old (about 13 years), informal, rambling with auto-caption garbling; tools mentioned may have changed.
